title: Trace Hypothesis Runner: auto-generate PagerDuty runbooks + Slack quick-actions from span signals
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Problem: When incidents trigger from latency or error spikes, on-call engineers spend 5–15 minutes manually reading traces, correlating spans to recent deploys, and composing an initial remediation playbook. Our goal is to reduce that cognitive and time overhead by auto-producing an actionable incident starter: a short evidence-backed hypothesis, a templated runbook draft attached to the PagerDuty incident, and Slack quick-actions to run containment or rollback steps.
acceptance_criteria:
1) PD incident receives an attachment named 'trace-hypothesis' containing a one-paragraph root-cause hypothesis and top-3 supporting spans with timestamps.
2) The attachment includes links to trace view + relevant logs.
3) A draft runbook (editable) is created and attached to the PD incident with 3 suggested run steps (contain, mitigate, escalate) and an estimated blast radius.
4) Slack incident channel shows quick-actions (button to run containment play, add note, escalate to SRE lead).
5) On-call can accept the generated runbook in < 2 clicks and actions invoke idempotent operator API endpoints.
6) End-to-end tests simulate injected errors and assert time-to-first-action < 120s after notification.
7) Security review sign-off present for attachments and PD data-sharing flow.
tasks: Define mapping table: span-pattern -> hypothesis template (work with applied-ml)
Implement trace hook that synthesizes 3-sentence hypothesis from span features
Create PD attachment schema and API call to attach runbook drafts to incidents
Build Slack modal & quick-actions with safe operator API integration
Add logging & telemetry: track suggestion acceptance rate and time-to-first-action
Write end-to-end integration tests (synthetic traces + PD simulation)
Coordinate security review and update IRB doc for PD attachment handling
Document runbook templates and failure modes in Confluence

rollout_plan:
1) Feature flag behind 'trace_hypothesis_v1' default off.
2) Enable for internal SRE-only PD escalation channels in staging.
3) Roll to 10% of production alerts (alpha) and collect acceptance metrics for 2 weeks.
4) Gradual ramp to 50% if acceptance rate > 30% and no false-positive remediation invoked.
5) Full rollout after security & legal sign-off.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Incorrect hypothesis may cause confusion: mitigate by clearly labeling suggestions as 'assistant-generated' and requiring human confirmation before any high-impact action.
- Leaking sensitive data in PD attachment: encrypt persisted drafts and redact PII from traces/log snippets.
- Operator API misuse from Slack buttons: implement RBAC checks + auditing + idempotency keys.
- Model drift in mapping rules: schedule monthly review and add human feedback signal to retrain mapping heuristics.
success_metrics:
- Median time-to-first-action after notification reduced by >=40%.
- Suggestion acceptance rate >= 30% in alpha.
- Zero incidents caused by automated actions (safety).
- On-call satisfaction (post-incident survey) > 4/5 for incidents using the feature.
